messages.subject: M2 Function
parts:
Dear Phil,

I will soon be conducting a research for my diploma thesis and I plan to use the mirt package to do the analyses. However, I have some questions regarding the M2 function in the package:

1) If I know that the items in my questionnaire will have 5 response options (Likert-type scale) and that I will use the graded response model, is it possible to estimate how many items/responses are needed for mirt to calculate M2 (i.e. in order for mirt not to tell me that the number of df is too low)?

2) Some time before you talked about a hybrid approach to calculating M2. Could you point me to some literature regarding this?

Thanks,
AM

parts:
On Tue, Feb 6, 2018 at 9:57 AM, AM <mut...@gmail.com> wrote:
Dear Phil,

I will soon be conducting a research for my diploma thesis and I plan to use the mirt package to do the analyses. However, I have some questions regarding the M2 function in the package:

1) If I know that the items in my questionnaire will have 5 response options (Likert-type scale) and that I will use the graded response model, is it possible to estimate how many items/responses are needed for mirt to calculate M2 (i.e. in order for mirt not to tell me that the number of df is too low)?

There are J*(J+1)/2, where J = # of items, df available for the M2* statistic. So this would to be larger than the p total parameters estimated in the IRT models. This is often why it doesn't work so well for smaller tests, because for a 4 item model with say 16 parameters estimated is not possible.
2) Some time before you talked about a hybrid approach to calculating M2. Could you point me to some literature regarding this?

I've seen a technical report written by Li Cai on this, but I imagine it's been published by now. He calls the hybrid the C2 statistic, which is essentially a hybrid between M2 and M2*. If I ever find time to write out the full M2 statistic, then C2 is a simple extension. But writing out the moments efficiently in C++ code is a pain (volunteers here are welcome). HTH.
 

Thanks,
AM
